clinician.final_diagnosis: a stage IIIC germ cell tumor
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old transgender patient presented with progressive right-sided scrotal swelling, abdominal/back pain, fatigue, and weight loss. Initial workup included a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, which revealed a right groin lesion, a large retroperitoneal mass causing hydronephrosis, extensive deep vein thrombosis, and widespread lymphadenopathy (celiac axis, retrocrural space, external iliac chains, left-side neck). Serum tumor markers showed significantly elevated LDH (5294 U/L) and beta-hCG (2526 IU/L), with normal AFP (< 2.5 μg/L). Based on these findings, chemotherapy with bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin (BEP) was initiated, and hormonal therapy was discontinued. Several months later, a radical right inguinal orchiectomy was performed, with pathology revealing scarring related to treatment effect but no evidence of malignancy. Post-treatment tumor markers normalized (AFP 2.7 μg/L, β-HCG 2.4 IU/L, and LDH 247 U/L).

CT scan of the thorax revealed left-side neck adenopathy (3 × 3 cm).
